concepts.title: Fraction of a Sector in a Pie Chart
concepts.definition: The relative size of a category in a circular display compared to the overall aggregate amount.
concepts.key_idea: The fraction represents the ratio of a component to the entire data set.
question_patterns: find the fraction of the circle representing each category
what fraction of the pie chart corresponds to this activity
calculate the proportion of the sector for the given value
determine the fractional part of the circle for the component
What portion of the day does a 6-hour school block take?

solution_steps.action: divide component value by total value
solution_steps.explain: sector fraction is the component divided by the total

concepts.title: Central Angle of a Sector
concepts.definition: The angle formed at the circle center proportional to a particular category's share of the complete 360 degrees.
concepts.key_idea: Distributing the full 360-degree rotation according to data shares.
question_patterns: find the central angle of each sector
calculate the sector angle for the given category
what is the central angle corresponding to the component
compute the angle subtended at the centre for this value
Convert a 30-unit share of 120 into a slice angle.

solution_steps.explain: find the proportion of the category out of the total
scale the fraction to the entire 360 degrees of the circle

concepts.title: Central Angle from Percentage
concepts.definition: Given the share as a percent, turn that percent into the corner angle of its slice.
concepts.key_idea: Convert percentage to a degree measurement out of 360 degrees.
question_patterns: find the central angle for a given percentage
calculate the sector angle corresponding to percentage
what is the angle in degrees for the given percent share
compute the central angle for percentage of students
Draw the slice for 25 percent -- what angle do you cut?

solution_steps.explain: multiply percentage by 360 and divide by 100

concepts.title: Category Value from Central Angle
concepts.definition: Determining the actual quantity or score represented by a sector using its central angle and the total sum.
concepts.key_idea: Scale the total quantity by the ratio of the sector's central angle to 360 degrees.
question_patterns: find the value corresponding to central angle
how many marks were obtained if the central angle is given
calculate the quantity represented by the sector angle
what is the actual value for the sector with central angle
A 60-degree slice of a 600-mango chart -- how many mangoes?

solution_steps.explain: divide the central angle by 360 degrees
multiply the angle fraction by total value

concepts.title: Total Quantity from Part Value and Percentage
concepts.definition: Finding the grand total when a specific part's value and its percentage share are known.
concepts.key_idea: The total is obtained by scaling the component value by the reciprocal of its percentage.
question_patterns: if a percentage represents a given value find the total
calculate the total number of people surveyed given part count and percentage
find the total expenditure given monthly savings and savings percentage
how many total items are there given one category count and percent
20 percent of a class is 9 students -- how big is the class?

solution_steps.explain: divide the given part value by percentage and multiply by 100

concepts.title: Theoretical Probability of an Event
concepts.definition: Favourable count over total count of same-likely outcomes gives the chance of an event.
concepts.key_idea: When every outcome carries the same weight, the chance is its fair share of the total.
question_patterns: find the probability of getting an outcome
calculate the probability of drawing a specific item
what is the probability of the pointer stopping on a letter
determine the chance of rolling a prime number on a die
A spinner has 8 equal sectors with 3 shaded -- chance of landing shaded?
One card is drawn from 52 -- chance of an ace?

solution_steps.action: divide favorable outcomes by total outcomes
solution_steps.explain: probability is favorable outcomes divided by total outcomes

concepts.title: Probability of a Complementary Event
concepts.definition: The likelihood of an event not taking place, given by the non-favorable outcomes divided by total possible outcomes.
concepts.key_idea: The outcomes not favoring an event constitute its complement.
question_patterns: find the probability of not getting a specific colour
calculate the probability of not rolling a number greater than 5
what is the probability of getting a non-blue sector
determine the chance of an event not occurring
One card is drawn from 52 -- chance it is not a heart?
The chance of rain is 0.3 -- what is the chance of no rain?

solution_steps.explain: subtract favorable outcomes from total outcomes
divide non-favorable outcomes by total outcomes

worked_examples.question_pattern: If the monthly savings of {part_value} represents {percentage} percent, what is the monthly expenditure on clothes of {target_percentage} percent?

solution_template.explain: divide part value by percentage and multiply by 100
multiply total value by target percentage divided by 100

worked_examples.question_pattern: The sales of ordinary bread are {category_value} out of total sales {total_value}. Find the central angle of the sector.

solution_template.explain: find the ratio of bread sales to total sales

worked_examples.question_pattern: A bag has {red_balls} red balls and {yellow_balls} yellow balls. What is the probability of drawing a red ball?

solution_template.explain: add red balls and yellow balls
divide number of red balls by total outcomes

questions: 1. A survey was made to find the type of music that a certain group of young people liked in a city. (i) If 20 people liked classical music (10%), how many young people were surveyed? (ii) Which type of music is liked by the maximum number of people? (iii) If a cassette company were to make 1000 CD's, how many of each type would they make?

2. A group of 360 people were asked to vote for their favourite season from the three seasons rainy, winter and summer (Summer: 90, Rainy: 120, Winter: 150). (i) Which season got the most votes? (ii) Find the central angle of each sector. (iii) Draw a pie chart to show this information.
3. Draw a pie chart showing colours preferred by a group of 36 people: Blue 18, Green 9, Red 6, Yellow 3.

4. Pie chart gives marks scored in an examination by a student (total marks 540). (i) In which subject did the student score 105 marks? (ii) How many more marks were obtained in Mathematics than in Hindi? (iii) Examine whether the sum of marks in Social Science and Mathematics is more than that in Science and Hindi.
5. The number of students in a hostel speaking different languages: Hindi 40, English 12, Marathi 9, Tamil 7, Bengali 4, Total 72. Display the data in a pie chart.
1. List the outcomes you can see in these experiments: (a) Spinning a wheel (b) Tossing two coins together.
2. When a die is thrown, list the outcomes of an event of getting: (i) (a) a prime number (b) not a prime number, (ii) (a) a number greater than 5 (b) a number not greater than 5.

3. Find: (a) Probability of the pointer stopping on D in a 5-sector wheel (A, A, B, C, D). (b) Probability of getting an ace from a well shuffled deck of 52 playing cards. (c) Probability of getting a red apple from a basket of 4 red and 3 green apples.

4. Numbers 1 to 10 are written on ten separate slips. What is the probability of: (i) getting a number 6? (ii) getting a number less than 6? (iii) getting a number greater than 6? (iv) getting a 1-digit number?
5. If you have a spinning wheel with 3 green sectors, 1 blue sector and 1 red sector, what is the probability of getting a green sector? What is the probability of getting a non-blue sector?
6. Find the probabilities of the events given in Question 2 when rolling a die.
